title: From Simulation to Reality: A Real-Time Platform for Operational Carbon Monitoring in Modular Integrated Construction (MiC)
funder: Environment and Conservation Fund (ECF)
details: This project aims to develop a blockchain-enabled IoT–BIM platform (BIBP) for monitoring and managing operational carbon in existing Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) buildings. By integrating flexible IoT sensing and blockchain technology with a data-driven operational carbon estimation model, the project will deliver an automated and trustworthy carbon monitoring platform that supports BIM-based carbon visualization and user interaction. The platform is expected to advance real-time operational carbon monitoring in MiC buildings.

title: Smart Embodied Carbon Management for Modular Buildings: Integrating Large Language Models and Blockchain for Real-Time Tracking, Predictive Analysis, and Adaptive Optimization
funder: Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Fund
details: This project aims to develop an intelligent and trustworthy system for quantifying, monitoring, and optimizing embodied carbon emissions in modular buildings. By integrating large language models (LLMs), BIM-IoT sensing, and blockchain, it establishes a digital twin platform to enable automated carbon accounting and real-time management, supporting the low-carbon transition of the construction industry.

title: Carbon Credits as a Catalyst for Promoting Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) in Hong Kong: Empirical Analysis and Policy Strategies
funder: Public Policy Research Funding Scheme
details: This project aims to identify the technical, regulatory, social, economic, and geographical challenges and opportunities associated with establishing carbon credit mechanisms for MiC in Hong Kong through a socio-technical systems framework, assess the carbon emissions and reduction potential of MiC products in case buildings, and explore potential carbon credit scenarios for MiC in Hong Kong. Based on the findings, it provides evidence-based policy recommendations for carbon credit strategies that support MiC development in Hong Kong.

title: Tracing and Optimizing the Embodied Carbon Flows of Modular Buildings in the Greater Bay Area
funder: Research Grants Council (RGC) General Research Fund (GRF)
details: This project aims to trace and optimize the embodied carbon (EC) flows of modular buildings in the Greater Bay Area. The project develops a multi-layer circulation network and models from the temporal, spatial, and sectoral perspectives for tracing the EC flows of modular buildings, investigates changed EC flows due to the adoption of modular construction (MC), and optimizes the entire EC flows of modular buildings using a hybrid Artificial Neural Network based Genetic Algorithm-System Dynamics (ANN-GA-SD) model. This project aligns with the global initiatives to achieve carbon neutrality and local government policies to promote MC. The findings are expected to benefit the whole building industry to achieve a low-carbon high-efficiency development.

title: Achieving Low-Carbon, Low-Cost Products in Prefabricated and Modular Construction for High-Rise Residential Buildings
funder: Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Fund
details: This project aims to assess and reduce embodied carbon (EC) in prefabricated and modular high-rise buildings. The project develops a multi-level assessment model to quantify EC emissions in prefabricated and modular high-rise building. Using real residential cases, the project then compares cradle-to-end-of-use EC emissions and identifies EC-intensive activities of high-rise concrete buildings using volumetric modular and panelized prefabrication construction. Following this, the project examines the drivers of identified EC-intensive activities and evaluates potential strategies while considering cost and construction time. The findings provide practical evidence for selecting feasible reduction measures and support lower-carbon residential construction.

title: Blockchain-Enabled IoT-BIM Platform (BIBP) for Quality and Process Management in Modular Integrated Construction (MiC)
funder: University Grants Committee (UGC) Carbon Neutrality Funding Scheme
details: The Blockchain-Enabled IoT-BIM Platform (BIBP) integrates blockchain, Building Information Modelling (BIM) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to support quality, process and carbon management in Modular Integrated Construction (MiC). The project develops connected hardware and software modules that collect RFID, sensor, GPS and energy consumption data and associate them with BIM models and project documents. A shared data management layer provides traceable records and supports embodied carbon quantification across material extraction, manufacturing, transport and construction. Integrated applications enable quality inspection, defect rectification, module progress tracking, and embodied carbon monitoring, supporting coordinated project delivery and decisions throughout the project lifecycle.
